calls.reason: Liang and colleagues demonstrate discriminatory detector errors, while Hendrycks and colleagues identify substantial misuse and deployment risks. These mechanisms do not require uncontrollable superintelligence.

Turner and colleagues provide conditional evidence of power seeking but explicitly limit its applicability to superintelligence. That single study cannot settle the broader claim about what researchers knew.

The Forecasting Research Institute finds limited grounds for extrapolating near-term accuracy to long-term risk. This does not settle whether precise doom probabilities will ever be calculable; Marcus gives no deadline.
AI Impacts measures risk beliefs, and Bengio describes disagreements. Neither establishes how much of the community was unwilling to discuss catastrophe or extinction risk.

The forecasting tournament documents disagreement, while titotal challenges one takeover mechanism and retains catastrophe scenarios. Neither establishes whether all arguments for negligible overall risk lack merit.
